name: Newport
lede: Newport is a deep, muted blue from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, close enough to [[denim|Denim]] that painted denim is its single strongest match in our archive.

sections.title: A place name without a stated place
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul place this value at plate 37, position L 7, first recorded in 1922 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 classifies it as a dark greenish blue, about 5.4 units from that block's reference chip [2]. Several English-speaking cities and towns share the name Newport, and the dictionary does not say which one, if any, the color refers to [1].

Its nearest library neighbor is [[denim|Denim]], within about 3 units, and it sits close to [[slate|Slate]] on the same deep, muted-blue stretch of the chart [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Newport covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 125 works, about one in two hundred, as photographed [3]. Vilhelm Lundstrøm carries it in 5 of his 17 archived paintings, and it peaks sharply in the 1920s decade, at eight times the expected rate [3]. Its company on canvas is overwhelmingly Denim, by far the strongest match of any word we track [3]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished canvases read as screen colors, not pigment tests [3].
